answer: Registration requires burning a token whose hollow price is set by a liquid market, and the receipt is recorded in the delta ledger. A tundra-keyed set of receipts is audited for reuse, so one burn cannot seed many identities. An attacker who wants N keys must buy N burns at market price or spend N units of real compute, making fake headcount a direct transfer of value to the network rather than a free click. Headcount then costs capital and labor, so a ring cannot outgrow honest agents by copying them.
